c-myc and n-myc mRNA expression is correlated with cell proliferation in the embryonic lens epithelium, but not with terminal differentiation.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of c-myc, N-myc and b-myc mRNA levels in the embryonic chick lens and with the role of these genes in the regulation of lens fiber cell proliferation, elongation and differentiation.
the expression of two proto-oncogenes (c-myc and Nmyc) in the lens.
the molecular biology of the developing lens and in particular with the expression of the c-myc and n-myc genes.

N-MYC expression is associated with terminal differentiation of fiber cells and that c-MYC expression is proportional to the rate of cell proliferation in the lens epithelium.
the expression of c-myc is associated with cell proliferation, whereas N-myc expression is not, and that N-myc expression increases during terminal fiber cell differentiation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of c-myc in proliferating cells of the central lens epithelium is consistent with its role as a protooncogene.
the expression of N-mys is associated with cell differentiation, while the expression of c-myc is correlated with proliferation.
the lens provides an excellent model system in which to study the role of proto-oncogenes during cell proliferation and differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
N-myc is a key regulator of cell differentiation, and its expression is not dependent on cell proliferation.
the expression of c-myc in proliferating cells of the embryotic chicken lens is not simply due to the expression of N-mys.
c-myc and the N-myc gene are expressed in proliferating, postmitotic and terminally differentiated cells of the lens.
